transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Liu (Redwood CSM), Oliver Grant (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurora), Jamal Rivera (Aurora), Priya Singh (Aurora), Carlos Torres (Aurora)
Links shared: onboarding deck: https://redwood.app/onboarding/aurora_health_kickoff_v1.pdf, security pack: https://redwood.app/security/aurora_questions.pdf

Summary:
Short kickoff to align on onboarding timeline, infra prerequisites (VPC peering, service accounts), security/compliance asks, initial validation plan (sample traffic), and internal owners. Agreed to a pilot week and deliverables.

Topics:
- VPC & networking prerequisites
- SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
- Data retention and audit logs
- Pilot validation (latency and cost targets)
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone! Thanks for hopping on — I see we have most folks. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (Aurora): Maya here, thanks Samir — I'll be driving the project from our side.
[00:12] Jamal (Aurora): Jamal, platform.
[00:14] Priya (Aurora): Priya, security.
[00:16] Carlos (Aurora): Carlos, PM.
[00:18] Dana (Redwood CSM): Dana here, I'll be your CSM during onboarding, happy to coordinate.
[00:21] Oliver (Redwood SE): Oliver, solutions eng, I'll own the infra checks and perf run.
[00:24] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda — run through infra prereqs, compliance/SSO, pilot test plan, timelines, and owners. Anything to add?
[00:30] Maya: Sounds good. We're particularly keen on private deployment options — we may need VPC peering or a managed private plane, depending on security.
[00:38] Samir: Cool, we'll cover both hosted and private variants. For Aurora, is the preference for private from day one or staged?
[00:44] Jamal: Prefer private from the start for PHI reasons, but we can do a hybrid if it's faster. We need to see what the network setup looks like.
[00:50] Priya: I want to call out SOC 2 and audit logs. We need KMS integration and exportable audit trails.
[00:56] Dana: Noted. We'll send the Redwood security pack that lists SOC2 scope, encryption at rest, TLS, and KMS integrations.
[01:02] Samir: Oliver, on VPC peering — what do we need from them?
[01:05] Oliver: We'll need a CIDR range, firewall rules for the peering endpoint, and a service account with limited IAM perms. Also, if Aurora wants on-prem, there's slightly different steps.
[01:14] Jamal: We'll share VPC and a timeslot for peering. One question: does Redwood support transit gateway setups?
[01:19] Oliver: Yes, but sometimes routes get funky; we document the recommended route table changes in the runbook. I'll attach that.
[01:24] Speaker 3: (inaudible) routing can, uh, require a small change on your side.
[01:28] Samir: Thanks. On SSO, Priya — are you flexible on SAML or do you prefer OIDC?
[01:33] Priya: We use SAML enterprise SSO across the org, so SAML is preferred. We also need SCIM provisioning for groups if possible.
[01:40] Dana: We support SAML and SCIM; I'll include the SSO integration guide in the follow-up.
[01:44] Maya: Great. Next, performance targets — we need median latency under 120ms for assistant queries at peak. Is that realistic?
[01:52] Oliver: Depends on model and deployment. On Dedicated with quantized model and batching tuned, we can hit sub-100ms median for short sequences. For Hosted, latency varies by region — we can route requests to the closest region.
[02:03] Carlos: Cost is also a factor — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated in unit cost?
[02:07] Samir: We gave a high-level estimate in the pricing deck; Dedicated is more predictable and usually cheaper at scale, hosted is faster to start. We'll send a unit-cost spreadsheet.
[02:16] Maya: For the pilot, we want an apples-to-apples comparison: same prompt set, same throughput profile.
[02:20] Oliver: Agreed — we'll run a 3-day perf window, replaying sample traffic. We'll capture token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
[02:28] Samir: On data handling — Aurora will send sample prompts without PHI; we will ensure logs don't retain PII and show how to toggle retention.
[02:36] Priya: Need to confirm log retention defaults and whether audit logs can be exported to our SIEM.
[02:41] Dana: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to SIEM and we have a retention config. I'll include that in the security doc.
[02:46] Jamal: About model pinning and rollouts — can we pin to a specific model at route level? We want deterministic outputs during validation.
[02:52] Oliver: Yes, route-level model pinning and rollout policies exist. We also have automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity issues occur.
[02:59] Carlos: Any gotchas with KV cache or prefix caching? We've heard caching can mess with user-level personalization.
[03:06] Oliver: Good point — prefix and KV cache are per-session and we can scope cache to avoid cross-user leakage. There are some config knobs in the runtime. I'll document recommended settings.
[03:15] Maya: Timeline question — when can we start the pilot? Our engineering sprint frees up on 2025-04-21.
[03:20] Samir: That's doable. Propose we complete infra setup and SSO by 2025-04-18, then pilot the week of 2025-04-21.
[03:26] Maya: Works for us.
[03:28] Priya: One more security item — our procurement needs a data processing addendum and SOC 2 report.
[03:33] Dana: We'll attach the SOC2 cert and DPA in the follow-up.
[03:36] Samir: Good. On billing and contracts — do you have a PO timeline?
[03:40] Jamal: We'll need the PO for Dedicated capacity if we go that route, aiming to have approvals by end of April.
[03:46] Carlos: Also want a review cadence — weekly check-ins during onboarding?
[03:49] Dana: Weekly 30-minute syncs are fine, starting 2025-04-14.
[03:53] Oliver: For the perf run I'll need a sample corpus and traffic profile. Maya, can you share that?
[03:58] Maya: Yes, I can export a sanitized set by 2025-04-11.
[04:02] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk)
[04:05] Samir: Great. I'll summarize next steps at the end. Any technical blockers we should surface now?
[04:11] Jamal: Maybe identity — we'll need a SAML endpoint from Redwood and instructions for SCIM group mappings.
[04:17] Dana: We'll send detailed SAML metadata and an example mapping for groups.
[04:21] Priya: Regarding encryption — we need bring-your-own-key (BYOK) KMS support for certain data stores. Is that available?
[04:29] Oliver: We integrate with customer KMS for keys at rest for Private. For hosted, we have hosted KMS but can arrange HSM/KMS integrations for enterprise. I'll note the options.
[04:38] Maya: Do you have TLS mutual auth for peered endpoints? Some of our internal rules prefer mTLS.
[04:44] Oliver: We can support mTLS on the peering endpoint; it'll require cert exchange and slight network config. I'll add the steps to the runbook.
[04:51] Carlos: On observability — can we see per-route token costs and token-level latency traces?
[04:56] Dana: Yes, the Console exposes token-level breakdowns and trace hooks. We can give a demo during the next sync.
[05:02] Samir: Perfect. Anything else from Aurora?
[05:04] Maya: Not at this time.
[05:05] Jamal: No.
[05:06] Priya: I'm good.
[05:08] Samir: Okay quick recap — Samir to send onboarding checklist, SSO doc, pricing spreadsheet; Dana to create Trello board and share security pack; Oliver to send runbook and perf checklist; Aurora will share VPC details and sanitized prompt set. Target infra ready by 2025-04-18 and pilot week of 2025-04-21.
[05:28] Dana: I'll schedule weekly 30-minute onboarding calls starting 2025-04-14 and send calendar invites.
[05:33] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[05:35] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and action items.
[05:38] Speaker 1: (meeting wrap)

Notes on transcription: occasional words unclear due to overlap; some proper nouns transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwood Dedicate").

End of transcript.

Recap (bullet form):
- Infra prereqs: VPC CIDR, service account, firewall rules, possible transit gateway notes.
- Security: SAML + SCIM, SOC2 docs, KMS/BYOK options, audit log export to SIEM.
- Pilot: 3-day perf window during week of 2025-04-21; target median latency <120ms; token-level metrics collected.
- Owners & deadlines: see action_items list above.
